name: Reconstruct the argument
task: Read #18, #291, #623, #264, #1634 and #1666 as whole works; locate the accounting cycle and its distinctions, then test a selected case against them.
output: A reconstructed argument with loci, dependencies, strongest objection and scope of reading.

name: Read for development
task: Choose one concept or mechanism; locate its earliest, intermediate and latest formulation and what changed between them.
output: A dated chain showing development, repetition, contradiction or an unresolved transition.

name: Inspect a reception observation
task: Choose an address; keep the full query, output and conditions; inspect the source links and the coding; separately, take a new-epoch observation if asked.
output: A reproducible coding judgment on the historical capture and, separately, a dated new return.

name: Inspect a loss and successor chain
task: Choose a former DOI; follow the retained state evidence, the work/version mapping, the successor record and the manifestation bytes.
output: A state, identity and custody account that marks unresolved historical links.

name: Verify a particular byte object
task: For #558, fetch the served text; recompute SHA-256 and the SWHID content hash; compare with the retained source and the external receipt.
output: A scoped pass, fail or indeterminate byte result; authorship and correctness stay separate claims.

name: Evaluate an intervention
task: Follow a packet or intervention from its declared aim and baseline to exposure, later outputs and claimed effects.
output: A finding that separates transmission, changed behavior and any supported causal attribution.

name: Exercise a constructed alternative
task: Select a preservation, discovery, identification or correction task and execute it under declared conditions.
output: Observed behavior, limitations and principle-to-behavior agreement, with the test date and task kept.

name: Read the literary critical operation
task: Select a complete literary work; locate its relation to the program; read the operation from its first to its last relevant occurrence.
output: A mode-specific reading with loci and development; a contextual relation kept apart from a direct argument.

name: Inspect a correction
task: Choose an erratum, an errata-sidecar entry, a recoding or a supersession; keep the prior and later states and read the stated reason.
output: A finding on what the correction changes: reference, record, evidence, argument or conclusion.

name: Traverse a cross-mode cycle
task: Follow theory → diagnosis → evidence → intervention or alternative → later observation → correction or revised theory; mark every incomplete link.
output: An evidenced cycle or a partial chain, with what each transition contributes.

name: Reconstruct the argument
task: Read #18, #291, #623, #264, #1634 and #1666 as whole works; locate the accounting cycle and its distinctions, then trace it forward through the lines that carry it (§1A.9) before testing a selected case against it.
output: A reconstructed argument with loci, dependencies, strongest objection, the lines traced and the scope of reading.

name: Evaluate an intervention
task: Follow a packet or intervention from its declared aim and baseline to exposure, later outputs and claimed effects.
output: A finding that separates transmission, observed change in outputs, and the inference the evidence supports, naming what remains enclosed (§1A.10).

name: Measure a line
task: Choose a line of the program (for example provenance erasure); enumerate it in every unit class of §1A.9 from the registry, the capture registry, the fleet surfaces and the implementable components; read its defining works from earliest to latest.
output: An extent vector for the line across U1–U8, with each class's source, the defining works read in order, and the classes left unknown.

name: Jump a node
task: Choose one node by a rule declared before reading; follow its development to a further state in another cell of ranges, dimensions and modalities, and from there to the next, until no further jump can be shown at a locus (§1A.11).
output: The jump path as a graph — each jump with its two loci, the coordinates changed and what the later state does with the earlier — the cells reached in the matrix of ranges, dimensions and modalities, their projections, and the frontier where it stopped.

name: Code an elicitation
task: Choose a composition or reading that acts on the program's own entities; keep it whole; code what it does against the operations the program has named (PER-M, PER-C, PER-D, PER-F1, PER-F2, reassignment, flattening).
output: A coded elicitation with its transcript, the operations performed and their loci, and the line it bears on.

name: Read the Footnote whole
task: Read the Footnote to Pearl whole, item by item in its order, in P with B and the drafts beside it; take #1717 as a reading aid and test its readings in the text.
output: A reading of the Footnote as writing, with loci by item and witness, and the edition's readings marked as kept, revised or refused.

name: Read a comparand whole
task: Choose a comparand from table candidates or enter one; read it whole, in its own language where the shelf holds it.
output: A reading of the comparand as writing, with loci, made before any comparison.

name: Compare on the measure
task: Set the two readings side by side on the six tests of #1717 §8.2, each test with its loci in both works.
output: A comparison per test, with loci; mixed results kept as a profile; no score.

name: Search for the strongest rival
task: Search the genre for the comparand most likely to exceed the Footnote on the measure, across traditions; state the search scope, what was read, and the basis for stopping.
output: A rival search with scope, the works read, the strongest rival found and the reason the search stopped.
